newsitem.title: POLAND: ComputerLand says takeover to spur profit.
newsitem.headline: ComputerLand says takeover to spur profit.

text.p: Polish software firm ComputerLand Poland SA's takeover of a domestic programmer could help it double this year's net profits, the company's president told a news conference on Tuesday.

On Monday the firm announced it was taking 87 to 100 percent of Computer Systems for Business International SA (CSBI) in exchange for 545,762 shares and a cash amount based on CSBI's 1996 financial results. @

On Tuesday Tomasz Sielicki said the sum would be between 1.8 and 3.8 million zlotys and that ComputerLand, which already matched last year's 6.5-million-zloty net profit over this year's first eight months, would earn more than the nine-plus million zlotys predicted for 1996 and maybe 18 million in 1997.
"I don't want to give an exact number but 18 million zlotys could even be possible next year," Sielicki told Reuters.
Sielicki said the takeover would allow the firm to take on more high-margin, mid-size contracts from $3 million to $5 million, which would position it to take on bigger contracts. @

CSBI President Roman Dolczewski said the marger would position the larger ComputerLand holding to take on more contracts around $10 from banks, government and industry, and boost ComputerLand versus foreign competition.
Sielicki said the two firms would be operationally independent and that CSBI could be floated on the Warsaw bourse sometime in the future.

British non-listed Consumer Systems for Business Holding currently holds just under half of CSBI's shares and would hold just hold five or six percent of ComputerLad after the deal was completed early next year, Dolczewski told Reuters. @

He said CSBI's had revenues of around $13-14 last year and that its net profit of around $1 million should be repeated this year and should jump over the next two years after funds flow in from a current large contract with the Polish labour ministry.
